body:
Update: Upon further inspection, it seems that this issue is only present when I call `swagger generate` on a swagger spec file that is the result of the `swagger flatten` command.

For those coming by with a similar issue, I solved the problem by using another open-source swagger file flattener utility: https://github.com/mohsen1/multi-file-swagger-example. 

Once I replaced `swagger flatten` with a call to this tool in my Makefile, my project built with the generated code I was expecting, with all child object validations present.

issue.title: No validation is called on body of array type parameter.
issue.body:
## Problem statement
When the body parameter is an array type, referencing another type, none of the validation is called.

Its possible I'm just defining it incorrectly (as I'm new to writing swagger specs), but I can't seem to get it to satisfy the criteria around [this line of parameter.gotmpl](https://github.com/go-swagger/go-swagger/blob/master/generator/templates/server/parameter.gotmpl#L203)

If the validation checking done [around here](https://github.com/go-swagger/go-swagger/blob/master/generator/templates/server/parameter.gotmpl#L209) is done it works correctly, sending back a 400 any "state" that's not in the enum. But it never gets into this section because it passes the [{{ if .Child }} check](https://github.com/go-swagger/go-swagger/blob/master/generator/templates/server/parameter.gotmpl#L203)

In the "Generated Code" section below, the Validate method for the `BulkUpdateState` type is created correctly, but never called in `BindRequest`

## Swagger specification
```
swagger: "2.0"
info:
  title: Bug? Demo
  description: Description.
  version: "0.1.0"
schemes:
  - http
produces:
  - application/json
consumes:
  - application/json
responses:
  200:
    description: OK
    schema:
      type: string
  400:
    description: Bad Request
paths:
  /someResource/:
    patch:
      consumes:
        - application/json
      summary: Update the state of multiple stuff and things at once.
      parameters:
        - in: body
          name: massUpdate
          schema:
            $ref: '#/definitions/BulkUpdateState'
      responses:
        200:
          $ref: '#/responses/200'
        400:
          $ref: '#/responses/400'
      tags:
        - SomeResource
definitions:
  BulkUpdateState:
    type: array
    items:
      $ref: '#/definitions/UpdateStateRequest'
  UpdateStateRequest:
    type: object
    required:
      - ID
      - state
    properties:
      ID:
        type: string
        x-nullable: false
      state:
        $ref: '#/definitions/StateEnum'
  UpdateRequest:
    type: object
  StateEnum:
    type: string
    enum:
      - todo
      - done
      - blocked
      - skipped
      - unenrolled
      - custom
```
## Steps to reproduce
- Generate the server based on this swagger.
- Add a handler
- Hit the /someResource route with a patch request, containing JSON array with states other than listed in the enum.
- See that requests make it to the handler.

## Generated Code

```
// BulkUpdateState bulk update state
// swagger:model BulkUpdateState
type BulkUpdateState []*UpdateStateRequest

// Validate validates this bulk update state
func (m BulkUpdateState) Validate(formats strfmt.Registry) error {
	var res []error

	for i := 0; i < len(m); i++ {

		if swag.IsZero(m[i]) { // not required
			continue
		}

		if m[i] != nil {

			if err := m[i].Validate(formats); err != nil {
				if ve, ok := err.(*errors.Validation); ok {
					return ve.ValidateName(strconv.Itoa(i))
				}
				return err
			}
		}

	}

	if len(res) > 0 {
		return errors.CompositeValidationError(res...)
	}
	return nil
}
```

```
// BindRequest both binds and validates a request, it assumes that complex things implement a Validatable(strfmt.Registry) error interface
// for simple values it will use straight method calls
func (o *PatchSomeResourceParams) BindRequest(r *http.Request, route *middleware.MatchedRoute) error {
	var res []error
	o.HTTPRequest = r

	if runtime.HasBody(r) {
		defer r.Body.Close()
		var body models.BulkUpdateState
		if err := route.Consumer.Consume(r.Body, &body); err != nil {
			res = append(res, errors.NewParseError("massUpdate", "body", "", err))
		} else {

			if len(res) == 0 {
				o.MassUpdate = body
			}
		}

	}

	if len(res) > 0 {
		return errors.CompositeValidationError(res...)
	}
	return nil
}
```

## Environment
swagger version: 0.13.0
go version: 1.9.2
OS:   Mac OS 10.13.2

issue.title: Schema does not initialize defaults in nested objects

labels.name: model
labels.description: Related to swagger generate model command

issue.body:
## Problem statement
Whenever a schema declares a default value, the corresponding generated structure is properly initialized, like in:
```yaml
parameters:
  - in: body
    name: myBodyParam
    schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        p1: 
          type: string
        p2:
           type: integer
      default:
        p1: abc
        p2: 12
```

However, when defaults are declared at a lower level, no initialization takes place, as in:
```yaml
parameters:
  - in: body
    name: myBodyParam
    schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        p1: 
          type: string
          default: abc
        p2:
          type: integer
          default: 12
```

It looks like the "schema" term used in the [json schema spec](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-fge-json-schema-validation-00#section-6.2) has been taken to the letter, making it equivalent to the swagger schema term.


## Steps to reproduce
generate server with structures proposed  as examples and submit uninitialized body

## Environment
swagger version: x.x.x  
go version: x.x.x  
OS:

Nested arrays should be fixed now for simple params and headers.
Issue on model objects (e.g. in: body) remains open.

All items mentioned in this issue should work now, except the in line body param issue.
This one is more specifically described in #1392.

issue.title: No validation is called when the object referring to the array type parameter
issue.body:
## Problem statement
The issue is similar to the Issue #1392 and #1093 but not the same.
When the body parameter is an under properties in object type, referencing array data type, none of the validation is called. But if we mark the body parameter required, the validation will show in the auto-generated code.

## Swagger specification
**Case : 1**
```yaml
profileCfg: 
           type: object
           properties:
               value1:
                   type: integer
                   format: int32
              value2:
                  type: integer
                  format: int32                    
profileCfgs:
           type: array
           x-omitempty: true
           items:
              $ref: '#definitions/profileCfg'
Profile:
           type: object
           properties: 
                  profileCfg:
                       $ref: '#definitions/profileCfgs'
```

**Case: 2**
```yaml
profileCfg: 
           type: object
           properties:
               value1:
                   type: integer
                   format: int32
              value2:
                  type: integer
                  format: int32                    
profileCfgs:
           type: array
           x-omitempty: true
           items:
              $ref: '#definitions/profileCfg'
Profile:
           type: object
           required:
               - profileCfg
           properties: 
                  profileCfg:
                       $ref: '#definitions/profileCfgs'
```

**Case 3**

```yaml
profileCfg: 
           type: object
           properties:
               value1:
                   type: integer
                   format: int32
              value2:
                  type: integer
                  format: int32            
Profile:
           type: object
           required:
               - profileCfg
           properties: 
                  profileCfg:
                       type: array
                       x-omitempty: true
                       items:
                         $ref: '#definitions/profileCfg'
```
                    
## Steps to reproduce

Generate the server based on this swagger
In the Case1, the validation will not be generated.

```go
func (m *Profile) Validate(formats strfmt.Registry) error {
        var res []error
        if len(res) > 0 {
                              return errors
        }
         return nil
}
```

In the Case2, the validation will be generated successfully.

```go
func (m *profile) Validate(formats strfmt.Registry) error {
      var res []error
      if err := m.validateProfile(formats); err != nil {
                res = append(res, err)
      }
     if len(res) > 0 {
                              return errors
        }
         return nil
}
```

In the Case3, if we remove the refer to the array struct, and without mark the area required the validation will still be generated same as the code in the Case 2. (Case 3 validation generation is by the fix in the issue #1392 and #1093.

So I think there may an issue that I have to mark the parameter required which it referring to the array struct if I want the validation to generate. Thanks very much for your help!

## Environment
swagger version: 0.13.0
go version: go1.10.2 linux/amd64
OS:  Linux Centos
